title: Safa and Marwa
hookLine: walking seven times between the hills, as Hajar ran

lines: SHE RUNS TO THE OTHER HILL.
cards: A woman stands on top of a small rocky hill, shading her eyes, looking out over an empty valley. Her water is gone. Her baby is crying below.
She sees nobody. So she comes down, crosses the low ground, running where the valley dips, and climbs the hill on the other side. She looks again.
Nobody. Back she goes. The woman is Hajar, and Ibn Abbas tells her story in Sahih al-Bukhari.
Today, the walk pilgrims make in her footsteps.

teach.h: THEN HE WILL NOT ABANDON US.
teach.b: First, her story, which you first met back on day thirty-nine. In Ibn Abbas's telling, Ibrahim leaves Hajar and their baby, Ismail, in the valley with a little food and water.
She follows him and asks: has Allah commanded you to do this? He says yes. And she answers: then He will not abandon us.
When the water runs out, she climbs Safa, then Marwa, back and forth, seven times, looking for help. At the end she hears a sound, and the water of yesterday's well breaks out of the ground.
Second, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ's comment, kept in the same report: that is why people walk between the two.
Her searching became their rite. Third, what the Qur'an says.

teach.h: SAFA AND MARWA, SIGNS OF ALLAH.
teach.b: In Pickthall's translation of surah two: "Lo! (the mountains) As-Safa and Al-Marwah are among the indications of Allah."

Jabir, in Sahih Muslim, says that when the Prophet came near Safa, he recited that verse and said, I begin with what Allah began with. So the walk starts at Safa, as the verse does. Fourth, the walk today.

The two hills are inside the mosque now, joined by a long covered corridor. Pilgrims walk seven lengths in all, and in the low stretch between, marked out for them, the men hurry, the way she ran where the valley dipped.
Look at who sets the pace. Not a prophet, not a king. A mother, alone, worried, doing everything she could while she trusted that she wouldn't be abandoned.
The pilgrims, whoever they are at home, walk behind her.

how: After tawaf, pilgrims perform sa'y: seven lengths between Safa and Marwa, starting at Safa and ending at Marwa, now inside a long gallery of the sacred mosque, with men hurrying between the green markers.

o: the walk between Safa and Marwa, seven lengths, after Hajar

games.q: you're Hajar. Ibrahim is leaving you and your baby in an empty valley. what do you ask him?
o: has Allah commanded you to do this?
games.why: she asks if Allah commanded it, he says yes, and she answers: then He will not abandon us.

practice: Choose two points, a door and a window, a wall and a chair, and walk between them seven times, counting as you go, quickening your step a little on one stretch in the middle, the way she ran.
If you pray, make du'a as you walk; if not, hold in mind someone who is searching for something right now.
